metadata.title: Temperature Converter
metadata.description: Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit with F = C * 9 / 5 + 32 and print one decimal place.

instructions.main: Convert 36.6 degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit using `F = C * 9 / 5 + 32` and print the result with 1 decimal place.
steps: Set `celsius = 36.6` (keep it as a float — do not convert it with `int()`).
Print `F: <value>` with exactly 1 decimal place using `"{:.1f}".format(...)`.

hints.message: Set `celsius = 36.6`, compute `fahrenheit = celsius * 9 / 5 + 32`, then print with `"F: {:.1f}".format(fahrenheit)`.
`int(...)` truncates the decimal part — keep the temperature as a float and round only when printing with `{:.1f}`.
Follow the formula order: `celsius * 9 / 5` first, then `+ 32` — multiplication and division happen before addition.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: The conversion keeps the float precision and prints 1 decimal place.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: The Fahrenheit value prints with one decimal place.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Store the result in a variable named `fahrenheit` and keep it a float (do not truncate with `int()`).
